_what: Everything the files core knows about the files contract and the folder it shows, as DATA (src/data.rs reads it once). The core names no operation, field, status, word or number in code: each is here. `call` is how one contract operation travels: through the engine's one door (POST to the computer's origin plus `path`, the locally kept-open door or the remote one alike), as the JSON-RPC message `body` with each `slots` value filled: the request's number, its request key (BLAKE3 of this device, the request's number and the time it was sent, so a send is never mistaken for an earlier one), the contract operation and its input (a name never travels in a URL: f1 bug 20). The door runs live-namespace's session with that operation (tools/live-namespace/mcp-tools.json). `answer` points into the door's answer: `result` the operation's answer, `refused` whether it is a refusal, whose `result` is then {code, outcome}, and `protocol_refusal` the code of a JSON-RPC error. `operations` maps each job of the core to the contract operation that does it; one the contract does not offer yet is null, and the core refuses that job as `not_offered` instead of doing it another way. `fields` are the names of the fields the core reads from a contract answer and writes into a request. `refusals` map a refusal's code (and its outcome, when the row names one) to the one OS-neutral problem set every shell maps to its own (src/errors.rs); `protocol_refusals` do the same for a JSON-RPC error's code. A refusal the rows do not name, and an answer that is not the door's, are `unreachable`, so the core asks the next computer (namespace_unavailable, namespace_origin_not_bound from a copy that may not write the real store, an outcome the door could not learn). No HTTP status is read: the door answers every refusal in its body. The folder a core shows (its root id, name and contract folder) is the shell's setup, read from the computer's row, so one computer may show several folders, one core each. `identity` is the content identity form (BLAKE3, the contract's `1f:` multihash prefix, tools/live-namespace/src/account_files/write.rs). `upload_id_hex_chars` is the contract's upload id length (write.rs validate_upload_id). The numbers the core plans with are the contract's own `bounds` call (operations.bounds), asked of every computer at once before the first job and taken from the first that answers. `absent_version` is the `expected_version` that says a name must not exist yet (account-files-routes.json `_folder`). Pins are the contract's own pin rule rows naming items (`pin_*` fields; the contract answers `kept` per name for the device that asks); ignore rules are the person's rule rows the core decides itself. `trash_id` is the OS's trash container, which lists nothing (deleted names go to the contract's set-aside tree, Recently Deleted). `item_facts` are the facts of one item an ignore rule may name, with the field kind that picks its comparisons (tools/formula-engine/rules/rule-operators.json `applies_to`); `item_kinds` are the contract's row kinds, which the facts' `kind` reads as well. `conflict_name` writes the plain name a conflicting edit is kept under, beside the other version: {stem}, {device}, {date} and {ext}; `conflict_name_again` the same when that name is taken too, with {n} counting from `conflict_first_again`.
